---
title: "AI Policy: The Three Zones"
---

This course treats AI coding assistants (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and similar)
as professional tools: you will learn to use them effectively and critically,
and you will also develop the individual fluency to program without them.

::: {.callout-tip icon="false"}
## Zone 1 — Weekly exercises and final project: AI allowed and encouraged

Use the **verify-then-use** workflow taught in class. You must be able to
understand and explain every line of code you submit. The final project
requires an **AI-use appendix** disclosing what you asked, what the AI
produced, and what you verified or changed.
:::

::: {.callout-important icon="false"}
## Zone 2 — In-class quizzes: no AI

Quizzes are where your individual fluency is certified. AI tools are strictly
prohibited during quizzes.
:::

::: {.callout-note icon="false"}
## Zone 3 — In-class exercises: AI allowed, partner first

Discuss the problem with your partner before consulting an AI tool.
:::

## Why this policy

Statistical programmers now work alongside AI tools daily. Banning them would
prepare you for a world that no longer exists; letting them do your thinking
would leave you unable to catch their mistakes, and they make plenty. The
course therefore teaches the skill that actually matters: **directing AI
tools and verifying their output**. Week 8 is a dedicated workshop, and every
week includes a short "AI corner" showing one good and one bad AI use for that
week's topic.

Free-tier AI tools are sufficient for all coursework; no paid subscriptions
are required or expected.

Submitting AI-generated work you do not understand, using AI during a quiz, or
omitting required disclosure is an academic-integrity violation.
